report.answer_text:
The captain, also called the master, has overall command of the ship and is responsible for its safe operation and the safety of its crew, passengers, and cargo. Officers carry out many day-to-day tasks, but the captain retains overall responsibility. (bls.gov)
| Main duty | What it involves |
|---|---|
| Navigate safely | Approve the voyage plan, oversee bridge watches, and adjust course or speed for weather, traffic, and other hazards. (onetonline.org) |
| Lead the crew | Give clear orders, assign duties through officers, and make sure the crew knows what to do in routine operations and emergencies. (bls.gov) |
| Keep the ship fit for the voyage | Oversee the ship’s condition and safety equipment, and ensure cargo is safely loaded and secured without compromising stability. (onetonline.org) |
| Prepare for and lead emergencies | Ensure drills are held and direct the response to fires, flooding, medical emergencies, or evacuation. (wwwcdn.imo.org) |
| Prevent pollution and ensure compliance | Implement the ship’s safety and pollution-prevention procedures, oversee required records, and ensure incidents are reported. (wwwcdn.imo.org) |
A key point: the captain has overriding authority to make decisions about safety and pollution prevention. For example, the captain can delay departure if conditions make sailing unsafe. (wwwcdn.imo.org)

9.1 The SMS should include procedures ensuring that non-conformities, accidents and hazardous situations are reported to the Company, investigated and analysed with the objective of improving safety and pollution prevention.
